bugs.summary: strptime() fails to parse %w of '0' in LC_CTYPE=C
bugs.creator: michaelchirico4

comments.creator: michaelchirico4
comments.text:
Created attachment 3774
Handle %w of '0' consistently in LC_CTYPE=C

r63319 introduced a boundary check for `w_strptime_internal` that was not mirrored in `strptime_internal`, so we get this difference in behavior:

```
LC_CTYPE=C          Rscript -e 'strptime("2026 0 0", "%Y %U %w")'
# [1] NA
LC_CTYPE=en_US.utf8 Rscript -e 'strptime("2026 0 0", "%Y %U %w")'
# [1] "2026-01-04 UTC"
```
I think this can be closed (r90447)?
comments.creator: michaelchirico4

comments.text:
(In reply to Michael Chirico from comment #0)
> Created attachment 3774
> Handle %w of '0' consistently in LC_CTYPE=C
> 
> r63319 introduced a boundary check for `w_strptime_internal` that was not
> mirrored in `strptime_internal`, so we get this difference in behavior:
> 
> ```
> LC_CTYPE=C          Rscript -e 'strptime("2026 0 0", "%Y %U %w")'
> # [1] NA
> LC_CTYPE=en_US.utf8 Rscript -e 'strptime("2026 0 0", "%Y %U %w")'
> # [1] "2026-01-04 UTC"
> ```

With `%U`, week 1 starts at the first Sunday. So, Sunday of week 0 doesn't exist. In fact,

    strftime("2026-01-04", "%Y %U %w")

gives `"2026 01 0"`.

On the other hand,

    strftime("2026-01-04", "%W")

gives `"00"`.

The added code in `w_strptime_internal`, which is supposed to fix Bug 15195, is wrong.

In the formula, `save_wday - w_offset` part is supposed to mean how many days _ahead of_ `w_offset`.

	  if(tm->tm_yday < 0) tm->tm_yday += 7;

should be

	  if(save_wday - w_offset < 0) tm->tm_yday += 7;

.

Alternatively, discard it entirely, but replace

    save_wday - w_offset

in the formula with

    (save_wday - w_offset + 7) % 7

.

    strptime(paste("2026", c("00", "01"), "0"), "%Y %W %w")

should be one week apart, `2026-01-04` and `2026-01-11`.

comments.text:
Once again, the the change to `w_strptime_internal` in r63319 is wrong and shouldn't be followed by `strptime_internal`. For `%U` and Sunday, `strptime_internal` is already correct. For

    strptime("2026 0 0", "%Y %U %w")

, `NA` result is correct and it is `2026-01-04` that is wrong.

What gives wrong result is `%W` and Sunday (Bug 15195). Similar to what is said by  https://stackoverflow.com/questions/14646406/r-conversion-of-week-number-uk-to-posixct-issue#comment20464275_14646756 , r63319 is a partial fix of the problem. It fixes week number 0, but later weeks are still wrong.

comments.text:
Created attachment 3971
guard strptime against negative week-zero day of year

Following up on the week-zero cases discussed here, OSS-Fuzz found an AddressSanitizer global-buffer-overflow read in R-devel. With `strptime("2026 0 0", "%Y %U %w", tz = "UTC")`, the week and weekday calculation produces a negative `tm_yday`. In both `w_strptime_internal` and `strptime_internal`, the month search then leaves `t_mon` at zero, and the subsequent `__mon_yday[...][t_mon - 1]` reads two bytes before the table. The OSS-Fuzz report is https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase-detail/4807144269217792.

The attached patch adds a guard after the week and weekday calculation in both parser paths, returning an invalid parse before the month lookup when `tm_yday` is negative. It also tests invalid `%U` and `%W` week-zero inputs in C and UTF-8 locales. The direct cases now return `NA`, and `tests/datetime3.R` passes under an AddressSanitizer build. The patch is based on trunk revision 90792 and dry-runs cleanly there.

Patch also at https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/pull/421

Thanks a lot, Kevin!

Indeed, your comment 7 seems perfect; I could easily reproduce (on a ASAN-sanitized version of R-devel) and the simple patch did fix the problem.

Commited to R-devel as svn r90799 
(and to be back ported to the R-4-6 branch: this report was just a few days to late to make it to R 4.6.2 )

     print(quote=FALSE, rbind(paste(" ", wdfmt),
             cbind(format(as.Date(paste0(yr,"-1-1"))+ -2:6, format = wdfmt))))
```

(In reply to Suharto Anggono from comment #12)
Thank you, Suharto.  I now understand what you mean, and you seem to know what to do,
to get the more back compatible behaviour which still fixes the bug(s) reported here.
As I needed some time, too, to understand:
Here's a repro code which has worked in "all" versions of R upto R 4.6.2,
but fails in R 4.6.2 patched and non-old R-devel:

```
(lt1 <- strptime("2026    0  1 4", "%Y %U %w %m %d", tz="UTC"))# "2026-01-04 UTC", but NA in R 4.6.2 ptchd, R-devel)
(lt2 <- strptime("2026 53 0  1 4", "%Y %U %w %m %d", tz="UTC"))# works everywhere
stopifnot(inherits(lt1, "POSIXlt"), identical(lt1, lt2),
          identical(as.Date(lt1), as.Date("2026-01-04")))
## ok: R 3.0.1, 3.3.3, 4.0.1, 4.4.1, 4.5.1, 4.6.0, 4.6.2
```

If it's not easy enough to attach a patch to bugzilla (see my advice in comment #4),
I'd be grateful if you attach the changed source file(s) `Rstrptime.h` (and maybe `datetime.c`)
in a private e-mail to me, so I can try it and add the fix to the R source.
